title: Kom Ombo
standfirst: Kom Ombo’s temple stands right on the riverbank and is unusual in being double: one half for the crocodile god Sobek, one for the falcon-headed Haroeris. It is one of the stops in our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: The double temple
paragraphs: The temple is built symmetrically, with two entrances, two sanctuaries and two sets of halls, one for each god. It dates from the Ptolemaic period.

sections.heading: The Crocodile Museum
paragraphs: Beside the temple, a small museum shows mummified crocodiles found nearby, linked to the worship of Sobek.

sections.heading: The visit
paragraphs: Ships moor next to the temple, so it is an easy walk. Many cruises visit in the late afternoon or evening.

faqs.q: How long is the visit to Kom Ombo?
faqs.a: About an hour, with the museum.

faqs.q: Why is it a double temple?
faqs.a: It was dedicated to two gods, Sobek and Haroeris, each with their own half.

seoTitle: Kom Ombo temple on a Nile cruise
seoDescription: Kom Ombo's double temple to Sobek and Haroeris, the Crocodile Museum, and how a Nile cruise visits them.
